Ok so I'm going to give a description of the paper that describes changes of 4,000 gene clusters in Rats that the article cites as its main source. It can be found here http://www.ehjournal.net/content/14/1/70 I think it is a great paper, and as a general skeptic of the negative effects of glyophosphate I am surprised and convinced by some of the results.

First, I noticed the rats they used are very cancer prone, but that does not appear to affect the results.
Second, there was not pure glyophosphate used in the study. The additive contained "adjuvants", aka other chemicals or antibodies. The author notes that their results will be different than someone using pure glyophosphate. These adjuvants are worse than glyophosphate, but since they are included in roundup, it makes sense for the researchers to not use the pure shit.

Principal Component Analysis, or PCA, was used to find differences between controls and the test groups. This is a very powerful method, but it will not find correlation where there is none. So the fact that the PCA they performed was able to distinguish between control/test groups expression data is alarming. You can see the data to do it yourself if you want here, I might try it this weekend if it doesnt require much pre processing: http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE66060

The difference between survival rates of control vs test does appear different in females, however the roundup fed test subjects appear to have a larger survival rate over two years than the controls. I'm basing these survival rates off these reported numbers: "Roundup-treated female rats showed 3 times more anatomical signs of pathology (15 in 8 rats) than the control group (6 in 4 rats)."
